name: Pastel Turquoise
lede: Pastel Turquoise is a muted, greyed blue-green fixed by the German RAL paint system in 1927, grammatically a softened version of Turquoise rather than a new color idea.

sections.title: A softened Turquoise
sections.body:
Our library records Pastel Turquoise as RAL 6034, one of the colors the German RAL paint-naming system fixed in 1927, with no further story behind the choice of "pastel" over any other softening word [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[grey-teal]], [[glaucous-blue]], [[light-dull-glaucous-blue]] and [[dark-ash]], at 3.9, 3.9, 
In ISCC-NBS terms this reads as a light greenish blue, and in Munsell notation 9.8BG 6.8/3.4 [1]. The nearest named color in our library is Ash, 12.3 units off, a looser match than most of our standard colors get, with [[turquoise]] itself the obvious sibling [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue-green in 107 of 23,781 paintings, 0.45 percent, more common than 53 percent of our named colors, as photographed [2]. It most often appears as a hidden color, buried in shadow rather than light, in just over half its appearances [2]. It is over-represented in France, at twice the archive's baseline rate [2]. The earliest dated example, a 1480 panel by Geertgen tot Sint Jans, sits 447 years before RAL's 1927 record of the name, so the match is a look-alike hue in aged paint, not a trace of the pigment itself, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
